column1: # A possible implementation order for P/03: a plan, not a norm or a reduction of the lesson checklist.
# Read every chapter and imported contract in full. Existing chapter reading dependencies on P/04, P/05 and P/08–P/10 remain.

# gate uses the P/01 grammar: tests:<chapter>:<cases|*>[:seams], accept:<chapter>:<cases|*>, vectors:<own package>, vectors:<owner>/<package> (a package of another owner with a consumers.tsv row whose consumer is 03-worker), code:*, build; checks separated by ;.

# Tests are kit stagetests through real SDK adapters. accept selects only the scenarios.tsv of the chapter, which the judge runs on the process stand; never seams.tsv. Earlier stage gates keep holding.
# code:* — the rows of forms/code-rules.tsv whose stage is this stage or a stage of a smaller n hold, under the closed dictionary of the code
# checks Platform/common/acceptance/forms/code-rules.tsv; the generation cycle checks them, not the acceptance; * is
# the only argument; a row is a data error when neither its stage nor a stage of a larger n has code:* in its gate.

# weight: relative 1–5. kit: parts that close the whole stage; none claimed here. parts: reused pieces of the kit; slot-capture generates the transition chooser, core calls it and implements YOURS procedures.
# A green build or a cache seam does not close the domain stand. Common vectors use consumers.tsv and the package README selections; run all assigned tables, not just the local creates-key package.
# Final P/03 acceptance, OS races and domain dependencies remain those of the implementation README and of the judge's acceptance. Missing dependencies are not PASS.
# depends lists earlier n; when=true is always applicable. worker_stand waits for P/04–P/06 and the last stage for P/08–P/10: named external
# lessons, not a made-up profile key.
# The accept scenarios of chapters 3.2, 3.3, 3.4 and 3.6 start the controller, the resource or the console (P/04–P/06): their gates stand at worker_stand,
# which waits for these lessons. An item stands at the stage of its subject, and its full-stand scenarios remain evidence in its text;
# worker_stand holds no lesson items: the subject of every item is the worker itself, only its gates need the neighbours
# This stage rule also applies to P/04.
# norms — elements separated by «; »: the sections of the norms, the forms and the packages the stage builds on (read in full, above), and the items of the readiness
# checklists of spec/*.norms.md (the lines - [ ] **P/03.K-MM**), written P/03.K-MM; each item stands in the norms of exactly one stage, the stage at
# which every subject of the item exists; an item at no stage or at two stages is a data error. The items of the system
# checklists of spec/*.norms.md stand at no stage: they need the OS, a host or several lessons.
